test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 10 May, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'** i.e.** 'Up'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"blowing up" **is a colloquial term often used to describe a sudden disaster or rupture. Here, it refers to a potential failure or crisis in the financial system.
 
• The term **'up' **properly completes the idiomatic expression "blowing up", which aligns with the context in highlighting the severity of the potential problem.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'**Gaming in the banking sector seems virtually impossible to eliminate. The only effective measure to end it would be to make bankers personally liable for losses, to remove the sense that their actions - their games – have no personal financial or legal consequences. It is this, rather than removing the cap on bankers' bonuses, that has the best chance of preventing the financial system blowing **up **again.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 'Option 1', **'on'** does not correctly form an idiomatic expression with 'blowing' in this context.
 
• 'Option 2',** 'into'** is incorrect as it suggests transformation or changing states, not catastrophe or sudden disaster.
 
• 'Option 4', **'off'** can sometimes be used with 'blow' to form an idiomatic phrase (blow off), but it has a different meaning (dismiss or ignore) which is not suitable in this context.
